The GI guidance mechanism addresses this.
*   **Pitfall:** Sparsity supervision during training does not guarantee exact activation counts at inference (e.g., target 0.20 yields ~19.5%).
*   **Time Complexity:** The selection process involves forward passes through GsNet (lightweight MLPs) and GI calculation.
GI calculation requires iterating over all pixels and overlapping Gaussians, which is expensive.
Training time may increase due to the additional loss terms and GI calculation.
*   **When to use:** When flexible deployment at different sparsity levels is required, and differentiable optimization of Gaussian selection is needed.

*   **When not to use:** When strict real-time inference with fixed sparsity is required without the overhead of training a selector, or when computational resources for frequent GI updates are limited.
The method builds on 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) [18] and utilizes Gumbel-Softmax [16] for differentiable sampling.

It models the selection as a categorical distribution using Gumbel-Softmax (a differentiable approximation) to enable stochastic sampling during training, which allows for gradient-based optimization. The text confirms this module is part of the FlexGS method (as indicated by the table headers and context) and is used to select active Gaussians.
